title: Moving the Line
endLine: To hold a new pressure, move the kidney's line or the intake.

scenes.tts: Last time, the kidney shed salt until salt out matched salt in, where its line met the intake. So how does anyone's pressure stay high for years?
scenes.narration: Last time, the kidney shed salt until salt out matched salt in, where its line met the intake. So how does anyone's pressure stay high for years?
scenes.caption: Last time, the kidney shed salt until salt out matched salt in, where its line met the intake. So how does anyone's pressure stay high for years?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset, rearranged: the renal plot now fills the LEFT 65% of the frame and about 70% of its height; the circulation loop sits smaller at RIGHT 35%. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: pressure marker WHITE; sodium (salt) GOLD dots; the kidney's line GREEN; the salt-intake line GOLD dashed; blood pale BLUE dots; sympathetic output ORANGE; vagal PURPLE; sensors CYAN. A moved kidney line, new in this film, is MAGENTA. PLOT, kept all film: x axis 'mean pressure (mmHg)', 85 to 125, ticks every 5; y axis 'sodium out per day', NO numbers, 'teaching lines' tag under the plot. Lines are drawn from the lesson's illustrative values on a hidden y scale of 0 to 300: normal kidney line GREEN, y = 10 x (pressure - 85); usual intake GOLD dashed at y = 150. They cross at 100, marked by a ring labelled 'out = in'. The WHITE 'pressure now' marker sits in the ring. In the loop at right: heart, vessels, KIDNEY with its outlet; GOLD salt dots enter at the top and leave through the kidney at equal rates; reflex wires at resting brightness. Recap motion during the first sentence (on 'where its line met the intake'): a faint ghost of the first film's RED clamp appears on the small arteries with a tag 'last time', a ghost marker slides from 106.7 down the x axis into the ring, then the ghost clamp and tag fade out for good (no clamp in this film). On the question, the WHITE marker strains to the right (up to about 115) and snaps back into the ring twice; white text across the top: 'How does pressure stay high?'
Title 'Moving the Line' fades in above the plot for 2 s while the question text fades out. The WHITE marker rests in the ring at 100; GOLD dots keep entering and leaving the loop at equal rates.

scenes.tts: Off the crossing, salt keeps draining or piling up. To hold a new level, the crossing must move. One way: shift the kidney's line ten millimeters of mercury right.
scenes.narration: Off the crossing, salt keeps draining or piling up. To hold a new level, the crossing must move. One way: shift the kidney's line 10 mmHg right.
scenes.caption: Off the crossing, salt keeps draining or piling up. To hold a new level, the crossing must move. One way: shift the kidney's line 10 mmHg right.
scenes.visual: On 'draining', a ghost marker to the right of the ring shows a GOLD shaded gap above the intake line (salt lost) and slides back to the ring; on 'piling up', a ghost to the left shows a GOLD gap below the intake line (salt gained) and slides back. On 'the crossing must move', the ring pulses. On 'shift', a MAGENTA copy of the GREEN line slides 10 mmHg to the right: y = 10 x (pressure - 95). The GREEN line stays behind as a faint ghost labelled 'normal'. A small arrow labelled '10 mmHg' spans the gap between them.

scenes.tts: Now the kidney excretes less sodium at every pressure. The crossing moves to one hundred and ten, and holds there, at the same intake.
scenes.narration: Now the kidney excretes less sodium at every pressure. The crossing moves to 110, and holds there, at the same intake.
scenes.caption: Now the kidney excretes less sodium at every pressure. The crossing moves to 110, and holds there, at the same intake.
scenes.visual: At pressure 100, a vertical GOLD bar shows the MAGENTA line sitting below the GOLD intake line: less out than in. In the loop, GOLD dots pile in faster than they leave; the pale blue fluid thickens slightly. The WHITE marker slides right along the x axis, the gap shrinking (timing schematic), until it rests at a new ring at 110 where MAGENTA meets GOLD dashed, labelled 'new balance: 110'. Salt in and out equal again. The GOLD intake line has not moved; a small tag on it reads 'same intake'.

scenes.tts: Another way: tilt the line flatter, pivoting on the old crossing. At the usual intake, pressure still settles at one hundred. These are teaching lines, chosen for easy arithmetic.
scenes.narration: Another way: tilt the line flatter, pivoting on the old crossing. At the usual intake, pressure still settles at 100. These are teaching lines, chosen for easy arithmetic.
scenes.caption: Another way: tilt the line flatter, pivoting on the old crossing. At the usual intake, pressure still settles at 100. These are teaching lines, chosen for easy arithmetic.
scenes.visual: The MAGENTA line slides back and transforms: it rotates about the old ring at 100 into a flatter line, y = 5 x (pressure - 70), labelled 'flatter'. The faint GREEN 'normal' line is restored to full brightness beside it. Both pass through the ring at 100. The WHITE marker slides back from 110 to the ring at 100 and rests there; GOLD in and out equal in the loop. On 'teaching lines', the 'teaching lines' tag under the plot brightens.

scenes.tts: Now raise the salt you eat, and the intake line lifts. Which kidney lets pressure climb further: the normal line, or the flatter one?
scenes.narration: Now raise the salt you eat, and the intake line lifts. Which kidney lets pressure climb further: the normal line, or the flatter one?
scenes.caption: Now raise the salt you eat, and the intake line lifts. Which kidney lets pressure climb further: the normal line, or the flatter one?
scenes.visual: The GOLD dashed intake line rises from y = 150 to y = 250 (no numbers on screen), labelled 'more salt'; the old intake stays as a faint dashed ghost labelled 'usual'. In the loop, GOLD dots enter faster. The two new crossings are NOT yet marked. Question card at top in white: 'Which line climbs further?' The WHITE marker waits at 100.

Predict pause. The question card stays. GOLD dots keep entering the loop at the faster rate; the GREEN and MAGENTA lines and the raised GOLD line hold still; the WHITE marker sits at 100. No other change.

scenes.tts: The flatter one. The normal line now crosses at one hundred and ten, a rise of ten. The flatter line crosses at one hundred and twenty, a rise of twenty.
scenes.narration: The flatter one. The normal line now crosses at 110, a rise of 10. The flatter line crosses at 120, a rise of 20.
scenes.caption: The flatter one. The normal line now crosses at 110, a rise of 10. The flatter line crosses at 120, a rise of 20.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. A GREEN ring appears where the GREEN line meets the raised GOLD line, at 110, labelled '+10'. A WHITE marker slides from 100 to it. Then a MAGENTA ring appears where the MAGENTA line meets the raised GOLD line, at 120, labelled '+20', and a second WHITE marker slides there. Two brackets on the x axis, 100 to 110 (GREEN) and 100 to 120 (MAGENTA), make the difference visible.

scenes.tts: A shallower line means more pressure change per step of salt: salt sensitivity. A real normal line is much steeper, because angiotensin two and aldosterone fall on a salty diet.
scenes.narration: A shallower line means more pressure change per step of salt: salt sensitivity. A real normal line is much steeper, because angiotensin II and aldosterone fall on a salty diet.
scenes.caption: A shallower line means more pressure change per step of salt: salt sensitivity. A real normal line is much steeper, because angiotensin II and aldosterone fall on a salty diet.
scenes.visual: On 'salt sensitivity', the MAGENTA bracket glows; label 'salt sensitivity' above the flatter line. On 'a real normal line is much steeper', a dashed GREEN line labelled 'real: steeper (schematic)' swings up from the ring at 100 to near vertical; where it meets the raised GOLD line, its crossing sits only a little right of 100 (schematic, no number). Small labels 'angiotensin II' and 'aldosterone' appear beside the kidney in the loop and dim downward (falling) on 'fall'. The dashed steep line then fades; the GREEN and MAGENTA teaching lines stay.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. In Guyton's framework, pressure can rest only where salt out equals salt in. So a lasting change needs a moved line, or a changed intake.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. In Guyton's framework, pressure can rest only where salt out equals salt in. So a lasting change needs a moved line, or a changed intake.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. In Guyton's framework, pressure can rest only where salt out equals salt in. So a lasting change needs a moved line, or a changed intake.
scenes.visual: Reset the plot to one clean picture: GREEN normal line, usual GOLD dashed intake at 150, ring at 100 with the WHITE marker in it; the MAGENTA line and raised intake fade out. Tag at top left: 'Guyton's framework'. On 'salt out equals salt in', the ring pulses and two equal GOLD arrows (in, out) appear at it; in the loop, GOLD in and out flow at equal rates. On 'a moved line', a MAGENTA ghost of the line slides right and back; on 'a changed intake', a GOLD ghost of the intake line lifts and drops back. Label under the plot: 'move the line, or the intake'.

scenes.tts: What moves the line? Signals that make the kidney hold more sodium at a given pressure push it right. Angiotensin two, aldosterone and the renal sympathetic nerves do this. Natriuretic peptides from the heart push it left.
scenes.narration: What moves the line? Signals that make the kidney hold more sodium at a given pressure push it right. Angiotensin II, aldosterone and the renal sympathetic nerves do this. Natriuretic peptides from the heart push it left.
scenes.caption: What moves the line? Signals that make the kidney hold more sodium at a given pressure push it right. Angiotensin II, aldosterone and the renal sympathetic nerves do this. Natriuretic peptides from the heart push it left.
scenes.visual: Direction only, schematic: no amounts. Three labelled tokens arrive at the kidney in the loop, one at a time: 'angiotensin II', 'aldosterone', and an ORANGE wire from the brainstem to the kidney labelled 'renal nerves', which brightens. As each arrives, a MAGENTA ghost of the line nudges right on the plot, with a right-pointing arrow labelled 'right: hold sodium'. Then a token labelled 'natriuretic peptides' travels from the heart to the kidney, and a ghost line nudges left, with a left-pointing arrow labelled 'left: shed sodium'. All ghosts fade; the GREEN normal line, ring and WHITE marker at 100 remain. The ORANGE renal-nerve wire returns to resting brightness at the end of the scene.

scenes.tts: Aldosterone brings sodium channels, called E N a C, to the tubule-facing membrane of collecting tubule cells. In Liddle syndrome, mutations leave more of these channels active.
scenes.narration: Aldosterone brings sodium channels, called ENaC, to the tubule-facing membrane of collecting tubule cells. In Liddle syndrome, mutations leave more of these channels active.
scenes.caption: Aldosterone brings sodium channels, called ENaC, to the tubule-facing membrane of collecting tubule cells. In Liddle syndrome, mutations leave more of these channels active.
scenes.visual: Camera dives into the kidney in the loop: one collecting tubule cell fills about 65% of the frame height, tubule fluid band on the left labelled 'tubule fluid', blood band on the right. The plot shrinks to a small inset at top left, still showing the GREEN line, the GOLD intake line and the marker at 100. On 'Aldosterone', a few plain door cartoons labelled 'ENaC' (no molecular structure) move to the tubule-fluid face and open; single GOLD sodium dots pass through them into the cell. On 'Liddle syndrome', a tag 'Liddle syndrome' appears and more ENaC doors appear on that face; ALL of them are open and passing sodium, and they stay open and active for the rest of the Liddle story (s11 and s12). GOLD dots now flow through faster.

scenes.tts: Sodium reabsorption is higher at any pressure. Volume rises first, then pressure, until salt out matches salt in again, at a higher level. One channel has moved the line.
scenes.narration: Sodium reabsorption is higher at any pressure. Volume rises first, then pressure, until salt out matches salt in again, at a higher level. One channel has moved the line.
scenes.caption: Sodium reabsorption is higher at any pressure. Volume rises first, then pressure, until salt out matches salt in again, at a higher level. One channel has moved the line.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back out of the cell to the loop; a small icon of the cell with its many OPEN ENaC doors stays pinned on the kidney, labelled 'more ENaC active', all doors still open. The plot grows back to full size. On 'higher at any pressure', the GREEN line gives way to a MAGENTA line shifted right (schematic shift, no number), labelled 'Liddle'. On 'volume rises first', the pale blue fluid in the loop thickens while the WHITE marker is still at 100; on 'then pressure', the marker slides right to the new crossing of MAGENTA with the usual GOLD intake (no number on screen), labelled 'higher balance'. GOLD in and out equal again. On 'moved the line', the MAGENTA line pulses.

scenes.tts: Most human hypertension is essential, with many causes. The working model: the kidney's line is shifted right, flattened, or both. In people, that is hard to measure directly.
scenes.narration: Most human hypertension is essential, with many causes. The working model: the kidney's line is shifted right, flattened, or both. In people, that is hard to measure directly.
scenes.caption: Most human hypertension is essential, with many causes. The working model: the kidney's line is shifted right, flattened, or both. In people, that is hard to measure directly.
scenes.visual: The Liddle story ends: the 'Liddle' label and the pinned ENaC icon fade out, and the MAGENTA line returns to the GREEN normal position. Label at top: 'essential hypertension: working model'. Three small ghost variants of the line appear in turn from the GREEN line: shifted right, flattened about a pivot below the shown intake line (so it crosses the intake line to the right of 100), and both together; each is drawn MAGENTA and dashed. On 'hard to measure directly', a translucent haze settles over the three ghosts and a small tag reads 'hard to measure in people'.

scenes.tts: And a moved line tells you where balance lies, not what moved it. The kidney itself, its nerves, or hormones could each be the cause.
scenes.narration: And a moved line tells you where balance lies, not what moved it. The kidney itself, its nerves, or hormones could each be the cause.
scenes.caption: And a moved line tells you where balance lies, not what moved it. The kidney itself, its nerves, or hormones could each be the cause.
scenes.visual: One MAGENTA shifted line remains, with its ring and the WHITE marker in it, labelled 'where balance lies'. Beside it a large question mark labelled 'what moved it?'. In the loop, three candidates light in turn, each with a short label: the kidney itself ('kidney'), the ORANGE wire to the kidney ('nerves', brightening then returning to resting), and the hormone tokens from s10 ('hormones'). None is chosen; the question mark stays.

scenes.tts: So in this framework, every lasting level is written in salt. Whatever holds pressure somewhere new works through what the kidney lets go, or what comes in.
scenes.narration: So in this framework, every lasting level is written in salt. Whatever holds pressure somewhere new works through what the kidney lets go, or what comes in.
scenes.caption: So in this framework, every lasting level is written in salt. Whatever holds pressure somewhere new works through what the kidney lets go, or what comes in.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world. The question mark fades. On 'what the kidney lets go', the MAGENTA line and the kidney outlet pulse together, GOLD dots leaving; on 'what comes in', the GOLD intake line and the GOLD dots entering at the top of the loop pulse together. The WHITE marker rests in the ring, salt in and out equal.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (GOLD salt dots entering and leaving the loop at equal rates, blood dots circulating). Large white text, centred: 'To hold a new pressure, move the kidney's line or the intake.'
